limitations: Many object IDs vary by version or are contextual variants.
The full catalogue includes lots of decorative blocks, triggers, spawn objects, items and objects added in 2.2.
Unimplemented objects are rendered as markers and do not receive invented collisions.

physics_reference.target_version: Geometry Dash 2.2081 (Windows/Steam), constantes recuperadas por ingeniería inversa comunitaria; no son parámetros oficiales publicados por RobTop

collision_models_in_this_project.ordinary_spike: Small rotated rectangular hitbox, narrower and shorter than the visible spike and shifted upward toward its tip; approximate per-version calibration.
collision_models_in_this_project.saw: Circle-vs-player-rectangle hitbox using ID-specific approximate radii; includes saw/spike-wheel/gear-blade families, excluding the 918 large beast hazard.
collision_models_in_this_project.black_hazards: Classified by community IDs into rectangle, slope-triangle, or circle families; variants are approximate.
collision_models_in_this_project.blocks: Rectangular collision for recognized block families, with approximate half-height, small-square, and three-quarter-width dimensions for selected IDs.
collision_models_in_this_project.slopes: Triangle collision and approximate surface landing for a subset of standard and themed slope IDs.
collision_models_in_this_project.invisible_objects: Invisible spike, blade, square, slab and slope IDs keep collision but hide the artwork.
collision_models_in_this_project.orbs_portals_pads: Activation areas are approximate; mirror and linked teleport behavior and many trigger combinations are not fully replicated.

notes: IDs with aliases are version-dependent; the old and new ID can refer to the same visual family.
IDs 397, 398 and 399 map to spike blades 1708, 1709 and 1710; they must not be treated as saws.
IDs 406–408 are grass decorations in the community catalogue and are not deadly hazards.
Unimplemented IDs are rendered as markers and do not receive an invented collision response.
